english: For real numbers $\lambda$, $\mu$ and $\nu$, consider the system of equations

Let $\Delta$ be the determinant of its coefficient matrix, and let $\Delta_1$, $\Delta_2$, $\Delta_3$ be the determinants obtained from $\Delta$ by replacing its first, second and third column, respectively, by the column of constants. Suppose that $\Delta=\Delta_1=\Delta_2=\Delta_3=0$ and that the system has no solution. Then the value of $\lambda\mu$ is ______.
hindi: वास्तविक संख्याओं $\lambda$, $\mu$ तथा $\nu$ के लिए समीकरण निकाय

पर विचार कीजिए। माना कि $\Delta$ इसके गुणांक आव्यूह का सारणिक है तथा $\Delta_1$, $\Delta_2$, $\Delta_3$ वे सारणिक हैं जो $\Delta$ के क्रमशः पहले, दूसरे तथा तीसरे स्तम्भ को अचरों के स्तम्भ से बदलने पर प्राप्त होते हैं। माना कि $\Delta=\Delta_1=\Delta_2=\Delta_3=0$ है तथा निकाय का कोई हल नहीं है। तब $\lambda\mu$ का मान ______ है।
solution: If the coefficient matrix had rank $2$, two of its columns $C_i,C_j$ would be independent; $\Delta_k=0$ (third column replaced) puts the constant column in their span, so a solution would exist
Hence the rank is $1$: all three rows are proportional, i.e. the three planes are parallel (Cramer's test cannot see this case)
Then $x-2y+z=1$ and $x-2y+z=\frac23$ are disjoint, so indeed no solution, and every $\Delta_i$ has two proportional columns, so all vanish
solution_full: Cramer's rule decides the system only when $\Delta\ne0$. When $\Delta=\Delta_1=\Delta_2=\Delta_3=0$ the system may have infinitely many solutions or none.

Suppose the coefficient matrix has rank $2$. Then two of its columns, say $C_i$ and $C_j$, are linearly independent. The determinant $\Delta_k$ with the remaining column $C_k$ replaced by the constant column $B$ is $\det[\dots C_i\dots C_j\dots B\dots]=0$, so $B$ is a combination of $C_i$ and $C_j$, and a solution exists (with the $k$-th unknown $0$). This contradicts 'no solution'.
The rank is not $0$, so it is $1$: every row is a multiple of one row, i.e. the three planes are parallel.
The third row $(-2,4,-2)=-2(1,-2,1)$. Proportionality with the first row $(1,\lambda,1)$ forces $\lambda=-2$.
The second row $(3,-6,\mu)$ must be $3(1,-2,1)$, so $\mu=3$.

Check: with $\lambda=-2$, $\mu=3$ the equations are $x-2y+z=1$, $x-2y+z=\frac23$, $x-2y+z=-\frac{\nu}{2}$; the first two planes are parallel and disjoint, so there is no solution for any $\nu$. All columns of the coefficient matrix are multiples of $(1,3,-2)^{T}$, so each $\Delta_i$ has two proportional columns and equals $0$.
Other solutions of $\Delta=\Delta_1=\Delta_2=\Delta_3=0$ (such as $\lambda=-2$, $\nu=-2$ with $\mu\ne3$) have rank $2$ and infinitely many solutions, so they are excluded.
originality_note: New: the failure case of Cramer's rule, where all four determinants vanish yet the system is inconsistent; the student must prove this forces rank one (three parallel planes) and read the parameters from proportional rows (way 4). Closest known: 'if Delta = Delta_1 = Delta_2 = Delta_3 = 0 the system has infinitely many or no solutions', usually quoted without proof. Different because: here the inconsistency is given and the parameters must be derived from it, with rank-two cases ruled out.
blueprint_concepts: Solving system of linear equations when all three planes are parallel and disjoint

concept_use.Solving system of linear equations when: The conditions Delta = Delta_1 = Delta_2 = Delta_3 = 0 come from Cramer's rule; if the rank were 2 a vanishing Delta_k would make the system consistent.
concept_use.Cramer's rule: Inconsistency with all four determinants zero means rank 1, i.e. the three planes are parallel and (at least two) disjoint; proportional rows give lambda = -2, mu = 3.

stem_review: Read as a student: lambda, mu, nu real; Delta and Delta_i defined in the stem; nu is not determined, but the answer lambda mu does not depend on it. Checked with sympy all solutions of the four determinant equations and their ranks: only lambda = -2, mu = 3 gives no solution. Answer -6, a negative integer as planned. Changed: No change.
key_step: All Cramer determinants zero plus no solution forces rank 1, so the rows are proportional: lambda = -2, mu = 3.
justification: The coaching fact 'all determinants zero and no solution means parallel planes' plus reading off proportional rows; short, but the justification needs a moment's thought. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q7 (L1) on consistency, with one more stage; L2.
